It looks like a race condition error for me. I got the errors if I loaded my resources with:

`((PackedScene)ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedGet(_SceneResourcePath)).Instantiate()`

I changed my code to something like this:

`((PackedScene)GD.Load(_SceneResourcePath)).Instantiate()`

And the errors disappeared. Maybe this helps somebody.

Yep, I can confirm the issue happens when using Arrays or Dictionaries with custom Resources and initializing them at the time of declaration.

You can still keep them as properties (`{ get; set; }`), but you need to remove any `= []` or `= new()` from the declaration.

Can confirm it works for my project too:
Remove **=new()** for all **[Export] Array** (Godot.Collections.Array) will get rid of all the Errors.
Don't forget if you have not yet assign any items into the array in the editor, you will get a null from it instead of an empty array like before.
You cannot initialize them on constructors either.

I finally had time to try this out on my other game and it also fixed the errors.  Should I close this issue, or leave it open because it feels like this is a Godot issue and the solution is a work around the real problem.

```
                EntityManager.gd:165 @ _unhandled_input()
```

When I have this uncommented in one of my files 
```
@export var secondary_animations: Dictionary[AnimationDataComponent, AnimationTiming]
```
Where the AnimationDataComponent is a custom resource class that has no _init() or _ready() anywhere in the inheritance tree from Resource to it, and AnimationTiming is an Enum value. Replacing the AnimationTiming enum value with a string does not solve the issue. 
This does not trigger if the dictionary is replaced with an array (I have plenty of those in my project). It also doesn't happen with any Variant Type as the key, only with an Object Type as the key (custom Resource in this case). 

Additional context, this is what line 56 in Entity.gd is:
```
components = data.components.duplicate_deep(Resource.DEEP_DUPLICATE_ALL)
```
And the problematic line is in one of the components being deeply duplicated.

The issue only happens on duplication, when the component is first initialized during game launch, no issue whatsoever. 
Similar to other people who reported this issue, it just doesn't do anything, and everything runs as usual. 
The dictionary is still visible in the inspector, although it is untyped. 

Edit: Also happens when I instantiate a new copy of the component manually
